records.title: Unresolved UAP Report, Iraq, May 2022
records.aaro_description: Two areas of contrast move together near the centre of the sensor field of view throughout the clip.

records.title: Unresolved UAP Report, Syria, July 2022
records.aaro_description: Fourteen seconds of dual-sensor footage from a military platform. The mission report described the UAP as moving from north to south, while the video shows an object crossing right to left through the upper right quadrant at about the five-second mark.

records.title: Unresolved UAP Report, Iraq, December 2022
records.aaro_description: Ten seconds of infrared footage from a U.S. military platform. The mission report characterises the phenomenon as flying west to east; the video shows an area of contrast moving from bottom left to top right of the field of view.

records.title: Unresolved UAP Report, INDOPACOM, 2024
records.aaro_description: 9 seconds of infrared footage of an unidentified object within the INDOPACOM area of responsibility.

records.title: Unresolved UAP Report, INDOPACOM, 2023
records.aaro_description: Nearly two minutes of infrared footage tracking an unidentified object in the INDOPACOM AOR.

records.title: Unresolved UAP Report, Department of the Army, 2026
records.aaro_description: Infrared sensor pans between two areas of contrast, rapidly zooms in/out, and cycles contrast settings. No observer description was provided with the original report.

records.title: "Syrian UAP instant acceleration"
records.aaro_description: Infrared clip AARO says was heavily digitally altered before upload (replayed at 50%/25% speed, inverted, re-zoomed) prior to reaching a classified network in June 2024; original raw excerpt runs 2:52.

records.title: "UAP USO Formation [CALLSIGN] (Mission)"
records.aaro_description: Infrared clip shows 4 areas of contrast in a formation, with multiple apparent video cuts and contrast/zoom changes; AARO notes it was digitally altered before upload.

records.title: "Cigar Shaped or Fast Spherical UAP clip 15 OCT 22"
records.aaro_description: An area of contrast moves across the field of view, shown in real time plus two slower replays. Digitally altered before being uploaded to a classified network in June 2024.

records.title: "Spherical UAP Erratic movement [CALLSIGN] (Mission) 2022"
records.aaro_description: The sensor tracks an area of contrast throughout, with intermittent framing. Digitally altered prior to upload.

records.title: "Spherical UAP over AFG in and out of clouds, 23 Nov 2020"
records.aaro_description: An area of contrast transits the frame, presented first with zoomed, sharpened, motion-tracked enhancement at reduced speed, then as the original unmodified footage.

records.title: "Spherical UAP pulsing over water [CALLSIGN]"
records.aaro_description: An area of contrast stays generally centred across three segments, with a brief sensor contrast-mode switch mid-sequence.

records.title: "Spherical UAP in clouds"
records.aaro_description: Infrared footage tracking a spherical contrast area. AARO flags this as a DUPLICATE of PR57b, which a different uploader labeled "East China Sea, 05 Jan 2023" - the sea named here (Yellow Sea) reflects one uploader's title, not a confirmed location.

records.title: "[CALLSIGN] (Mission) UAP"
records.aaro_description: The sensor tracks an area of contrast; three segments at 8x speed, stabilised original speed, and unmodified original, with quality degrading in the final section. Uploaded to a classified network June 2024, digitally altered prior to upload.

records.title: "NAG UAP 1 Jun 20"
records.aaro_description: Infrared sensor zooms/pans to track one area of contrast for nearly 5 minutes, applying a targeting reticle for a sustained ~3-minute stretch.

records.title: "Spherical UAP [CALLSIGN] 2021/04/12 obj 2"
records.aaro_description: Full-motion video and infrared footage; the contrast transits right to left, re-enters, and the sensor pans left and up to track it.

records.title: "Spherical UAP [CALLSIGN] 2021/04/12 vid 0"
records.aaro_description: An area of contrast enters from upper right and is tracked across the frame. After about a minute the sensor changes modes as the contrast becomes indistinct.

records.title: "Spherical UAP [CALLSIGN] 2021/04/12 vid 1"
records.aaro_description: Colour and infrared footage; the sensor tracks a high-contrast area through panning and zoom. Lacked established chain-of-custody documentation.

records.title: "Spherical UAP [CALLSIGN] 2021/04/12 vid 2"
records.aaro_description: The sensor tracks an area of contrast for roughly 50 seconds before panning away.

records.title: "AFSOC Kabul UAP Jul 2017"
records.submitting_command: U.S. Air Force Special Operations Command
records.aaro_description: An area of contrast enters the field of view at the left edge and exits right, visible for roughly one second of the clip. Uploaded to a classified network in June 2024 though recorded in 2017.

records.title: "UAP Captured by Fifth-Gen Aircraft, 20 Jan 23"
records.aaro_description: A sensor tracks an area of contrast, keeping it generally centred, which briefly moves in and out of frame from the top as the sensor pans; a second area of contrast becomes visible in the upper right at 48 seconds. Source note: the DVIDS Date Taken field reads 23 Jan 2020 while the title and IIR reference indicate 20 Jan 2023 — a conflict within the source record itself, recorded here rather than resolved.

records.title: "F/A-18 FLIR UAP"
records.aaro_description: Short FLIR clip from an F/A-18 briefly locking a reticle onto an object before losing track.

records.title: "IIR 1 655 S0301 23 / Eglin AFB Aircrew Observed UAP, 13 Feb 23"
records.aaro_description: The sensor pans to keep an area of contrast centred, cycling contrast modes several times; at 22 seconds the contrast loses distinctiveness against the background.

records.title: USAF ANG F-16C Shoots Down UAP over Lake Huron, 12 Feb 2023
records.submitting_command: U.S. Northern Command / Air National Guard
records.aaro_description: At about 20 seconds the footage appears to depict a kinetic interaction between two areas of contrast, the initial subject fragmenting in a radial displacement pattern. AARO notes the material lacked a substantiated chain of custody.

records.title: "31 AUG [CALLSIGN] Observes UAP, part 2"
records.aaro_description: Multiple areas of contrast move through frame; the sensor tracks one near centre as others enter and exit. AARO notes the material lacks a substantiated chain of custody.

records.title: "21 AUG [CALLSIGN] Observes UAP in Persian Gulf"
records.aaro_description: An area of contrast transits the frame; the sensor zooms and pans until the object becomes indistinguishable from video noise. Lacks a substantiated chain of custody.

records.title: "08 AUG 2020 [CALLSIGN] UAP observation"
records.aaro_description: An area of contrast enters the field of view and the sensor tracks and zooms repeatedly over roughly four minutes. Uploaded to a classified network in August 2020.

records.title: "May 05 2020 Gulf of Arabia [CALLSIGN] Dual UAP"
records.aaro_description: The sensor pans to track an area of contrast; several areas of contrast then enter and exit the field of view as contrast settings adjust. Companion clip to PR095 from the same event.

records.title: "[CALLSIGN] (Mission) - HD 2020-02-13"
records.aaro_description: Electro-optical and infrared footage; an area of contrast moves through frame with multiple pan, zoom and modality adjustments.

records.title: "May 05 2020 Gulf of Arabia [CALLSIGN] Dual UAP"
records.aaro_description: Multiple distinct areas of contrast tracked and magnified; the objects move in and out of frame before departing at lower right around 1:47. Longer companion clip to PR093.

records.title: "HH11 03 July 2018 UAPs"
records.aaro_description: Multiple areas of contrast enter and exit frame with tracking and zoom; the distance between the rightmost and the centre-left areas appears to increase. Lacks a substantiated chain of custody.

records.title: "Hi-Res: [CALLSIGN] Observes UAP on 25SEP19 at 2135Z"
records.aaro_description: Areas of contrast tracked and magnified across multiple zoom and contrast settings over roughly five minutes.

records.title: "UFOs in Formation over Persian Gulf?"
records.aaro_description: Extended infrared footage; areas of contrast tracked with progressive zoom and pan. Uploaded to a classified network in October 2019.

records.title: "Hi-Res: [CALLSIGN] Observes UAP on 25SEP19 at 1715Z"
records.aaro_description: Areas of contrast move through frame. Uploaded to a classified network in November 2019; lacks documented chain of custody.

records.title: Unresolved UAP Report, Middle East, 2023
records.aaro_description: Begins on a dark area of contrast; two bright areas transit left to right, the sensor zooms out to keep them in frame, then refocuses on the original dark area with a reticle overlay.

records.title: Unresolved UAP Report, Middle East, 2023
records.aaro_description: Two areas of contrast cross the field of view between six and seven seconds; one enters bottom-right and exits at the top, the other enters at the top and exits at the bottom.

records.title: Unresolved UAP Report, Yellow Sea, 2023
records.aaro_description: Electro-optical and infrared footage; IR tracking of an area of contrast, a switch to electro-optical mode showing a dark object against a blue background, then further IR tracking with zoom and contrast changes. A footage discontinuity occurs around 3:28.

records.title: Unresolved UAP Report, South China Sea, 2024
records.aaro_description: Infrared footage tracking an elongated area of contrast; a further zoom reveals multiple contrast areas forming a line moving diagonally across the field of view.

records.title: Unresolved UAP Report, East China Sea, 2024
records.aaro_description: The sensor tracks a centred area of contrast, which then exits the top of the field of view; the remainder shows repeated zoom adjustments with no observable content.

records.title: Unresolved UAP Report, East China Sea, 2024
records.aaro_description: The sensor pans to track an area of contrast, keeping it generally centred, with an auto-tracking reticle surrounding it from 12 seconds to the end.

records.title: Unresolved UAP Report, Yellow Sea, 2025
records.aaro_description: The sensor pans to track an area of contrast resembling a six-pointed star, keeping it generally centred.

records.title: Unresolved UAP Report, East China Sea, 2025
records.aaro_description: Tracks an area of contrast with black rectangular overlays briefly present; the sensor intermittently loses definition, pans several times and zooms to follow the contrast across the frame.

records.title: Unresolved UAP Report, Eastern United States, 2020
records.aaro_description: Supporting document DOW-UAP-D089 describes the object as quite small, moving in a constant direction, indistinguishable in shape, metallic in appearance with a reflective underside. AARO notes the media was digitally altered before being reported.

records.title: Unresolved UAP Report, Eastern United States, 2020
records.aaro_description: An area of contrast repeatedly leaves and re-enters the sensor field of view as the sensor pans and adjusts zoom to follow it.

records.title: Unresolved UAP Report, Eastern United States, 2015
records.submitting_command: U.S. Navy UAPTF (transferred to AARO in 2022)
records.aaro_description: An area of contrast crosses the field from right to left and exits the upper left corner, followed by a slower-speed replay. AARO notes no formal data handling practices for UAP records existed at the time.

records.title: Unresolved UAP Report, Eastern United States, 2020
records.aaro_description: An area of contrast becomes visible and is tracked by an auto-tracking reticle, gradually increases in angular size, then exits the field of view.

records.title: Unresolved UAP Report, Eastern United States, 2020
records.aaro_description: Several small areas of contrast enter and exit the field of view. An auto-tracking reticle engages on one while others periodically appear; the display then cycles between black screens and normal function.

records.title: Unresolved UAP Report, Eastern United States, 2019
records.aaro_description: Captured aboard a civilian aircraft. The accompanying debrief records the observer describing flight characteristics unlike anything seen in 28 years of Air Force and Navy service, and the object as small and travelling in a straight line at high speed.

records.title: Unresolved UAP Report, Western United States, 1996
records.aaro_description: An area of contrast transits the field of view, entering near the upper right corner and exiting opposite. The remainder is frame-by-frame repetition at standard and slower speeds. AARO notes the media was digitally altered before submission.

records.title: Unresolved UAP Report, Atlantic Ocean, 2016
records.aaro_description: The sensor zooms and pans to keep an area of contrast centred, then switches modes with a white reticle on it. Tracking stops and the object exits frame right before another area of contrast enters.

records.title: Unresolved UAP Report, Gulf of America, 2019
records.aaro_description: An area of contrast near the centre of the field of view, partly obscured by heads-up display elements, which the sensor zooms and pans to track; the contrast visually flickers. AARO notes a source at ambient temperature can appear to blend or flicker as auto-gain adjusts.

records.title: Unresolved UAP Report, Atlantic Ocean, 2020
records.aaro_description: An object described as a darker, maroonish colour, approximately 12 to 15 feet in height, travelling with the wind without manoeuvring — resembling a large, somewhat deformed balloon.

records.title: Apollo 14 Debriefing, 1971
records.aaro_description: First part of the Apollo 14 post-mission debriefing. Crew and debriefers discuss the light flash phenomena — a then-novel, now well-documented biological effect in which high-energy cosmic rays strike the retina and are perceived as streaks or flashes.

records.title: Apollo 14 Debriefing (continued), 1971
records.aaro_description: Second part of the Apollo 14 post-mission crew debriefing, continuing the discussion of the light flash phenomena.

records.title: Apollo 17 Crew Medical Debriefing, 1972
records.aaro_description: First part of the Apollo 17 post-mission medical debriefing. Two of the three crew members reported experiencing the light flash phenomena during mission phases including lunar orbit and surface operations.

records.title: Apollo 17 Crew Medical Debriefing (continued), 1972
records.aaro_description: Second part of the Apollo 17 post-mission medical debriefing, continuing the examination of the light flash phenomena.

records.title: 2025 Middle East Populated-Area Clip
records.aaro_description: Infrared clip showing an object crossing the sensor's field of view rapidly over a populated area; remains labeled unresolved. [Editor's note: this entry's source could not be confirmed against the primary record; treat with caution pending review.]

records.title: Unresolved UAP Report, Gulf of Oman, 2021
records.submitting_command: U.S. Central Command (AC-130J Gunship, U.S. Special Operations Forces)
records.aaro_description: An area of contrast remains generally within the centre of the sensor field-of-view. Part of the Gulf of Oman 'cold orbs' series. Secondary recording of an infrared sensor display rather than native sensor data, which limits fidelity. The accompanying intelligence report (DOW-UAP-D101) describes the objects as 'cold orbs' roughly four feet in diameter.

records.title: Unresolved UAP Report, Gulf of Oman, 2021 (1 of 6 clips, PR117-PR122 series)
records.aaro_description: Secondary cellphone capture of an AC-130J's infrared sensor display during a live-fire exercise. Accompanying report DOW-UAP-D101 describes 'cold orbs' ~4 ft in diameter; crew reported ~25 instances moving 250-1300 mph in formation, appearing to react when the aircraft fired its cannon.

records.title: Unresolved UAP Report, Gulf of Oman, 2021
records.submitting_command: U.S. Central Command (AC-130J Gunship, U.S. Special Operations Forces)
records.aaro_description: Two-second clip, the shortest in the series. Part of the Gulf of Oman 'cold orbs' series. Secondary recording of an infrared sensor display rather than native sensor data, which limits fidelity. The accompanying intelligence report (DOW-UAP-D101) describes the objects as 'cold orbs' roughly four feet in diameter.

records.title: Unresolved UAP Report, Gulf of Oman, 2021
records.submitting_command: U.S. Central Command (AC-130J Gunship, U.S. Special Operations Forces)
records.aaro_description: Captured on a cellular device pointed at the sensor display; the area of contrast becomes less distinct when the sensor switches display modes. Part of the Gulf of Oman 'cold orbs' series. Secondary recording of an infrared sensor display rather than native sensor data, which limits fidelity. The accompanying intelligence report (DOW-UAP-D101) describes the objects as 'cold orbs' roughly four feet in diameter.

records.title: Unresolved UAP Report, Gulf of Oman, 2021
records.submitting_command: U.S. Central Command (AC-130J Gunship, U.S. Special Operations Forces)
records.aaro_description: Part of the Gulf of Oman 'cold orbs' series. Secondary recording of an infrared sensor display rather than native sensor data, which limits fidelity. The accompanying intelligence report (DOW-UAP-D101) describes the objects as 'cold orbs' roughly four feet in diameter.

records.title: Unresolved UAP Report, Gulf of Oman, 2021
records.submitting_command: U.S. Central Command (AC-130J Gunship, U.S. Special Operations Forces)
records.aaro_description: Areas of thermal contrast move within the field-of-view across three time segments, with sensor adjustments at the 8-second mark. Part of the Gulf of Oman 'cold orbs' series. Secondary recording of an infrared sensor display rather than native sensor data, which limits fidelity. The accompanying intelligence report (DOW-UAP-D101) describes the objects as 'cold orbs' roughly four feet in diameter.

records.title: Unresolved UAP Report, Pacific Ocean, 2019
records.aaro_description: An area of contrast appears, disappears and reappears; the sensor pans and zooms to track it from 0:08 to 1:04. Not native primary sensor data — the secondary recording method limits fidelity and resolution.

records.title: Unresolved UAP Report, Pacific Ocean, 2019
records.aaro_description: Secondary infrared footage; the area of contrast is centred, then zoomed on before losing distinctiveness. AARO notes artifacts inherent to filming a screen, and that the media was digitally altered before being reported.

records.title: Unresolved UAP Report, Middle East, 2025
records.aaro_description: Electro-optical and infrared footage; the sensor pans to track an area of contrast from left to right across the background, keeping it generally centred.

records.title: Unresolved UAP Report, Middle East, 2023
records.aaro_description: The sensor tracks an area of contrast and then zooms in. Platform occlusions obscure portions of the display.

records.title: Unresolved UAP Report, Middle East, 2025
records.aaro_description: An area of contrast enters the sensor field-of-view from the left edge, transits left to right, and exits the right edge of the frame.

records.title: Unresolved UAP Report, Middle East, 2023
records.aaro_description: An area of contrast transits the frame from the bottom right to the lower left edge in the opening seconds; the sensor then tracks it centre-frame for the remainder.

records.title: "Slow-moving Objects", Western United States, 2026
records.submitting_command: U.S. Government Special Agent (FBI submission, case FBI-UAP-D032)
records.aaro_description: Thermal imaging showing two slow-moving 'black-hot' areas of contrast in infrared, captured by a U.S. Government Special Agent. Documented as FBI-UAP-D032.

records.title: Unresolved UAP Report, Middle East, 2025
records.aaro_description: Infrared sensor footage tracking an area of contrast through repeated magnification and panning changes. The accompanying mission report (DOW-UAP-D107) characterises the object as looking like “a white round orbit… moving as fast as 500 miles per hour.”

records.title: Unresolved UAP Report, Middle East, 2025
records.aaro_description: Infrared footage of six small spherical objects grouped together, described as showing agile directional changes at an estimated 480 mph. This is the clip most widely reported in coverage of the sixth release.

records.title: Unresolved UAP Report, Middle East, 2022
records.aaro_description: Electro-optical and infrared tracking of an object the accompanying report describes as travelling at various speeds between 80 and 180 mph, with multiple sensor mode switches during the track.

records.title: Unresolved UAP Report, Middle East, 2022
records.aaro_description: Companion clip to PR140 from the same 2022 Middle East series; object again reported at speeds between 80 and 180 mph.

records.title: Unresolved UAP Report, Yellow Sea, 2023
records.aaro_description: Short infrared clip; the sensor tracks an area of contrast held near the centre of frame. AARO states the description carries no analytical judgement as to the object's nature.

records.title: Unresolved UAP Report, Yellow Sea, 2023
records.aaro_description: Infrared sensor footage from a U.S. military platform tracking an area of contrast.

records.title: Unresolved UAP Report, East China Sea, 2023
records.aaro_description: First three seconds contain no discernible content; from roughly 4 to 46 seconds the sensor pans to track an area of contrast held generally centre-frame, then increases magnification while continuing to track.

records.title: Unresolved UAP Report, Yellow Sea, 2023
records.aaro_description: 57 seconds of infrared footage from a sensor aboard a U.S. military platform.

records.title: Unresolved UAP Report, Yellow Sea, 2023
records.aaro_description: Infrared footage of an area of contrast tracked across frame, with the sensor adjusting magnification during the recording.

records.title: Unresolved UAP Report, Yellow Sea, 2023
records.aaro_description: Longest of the five Yellow Sea clips in this tranche; infrared sensor tracking of an area of contrast.

records.title: Historical Film of Reported UFOs, Utah, 1952
records.aaro_description: The Tremonton film — a group of bright airborne objects filmed by U.S. Navy Chief Warrant Officer Delbert C. Newhouse on 2 July 1952, subsequently reviewed by Project Blue Book. One of the most analysed pieces of film in the history of official U.S. UFO investigation.

records.title: Presentation by Captain Edward J. Ruppelt, 1952 (audio)
records.aaro_description: The sole audio file in this tranche and a long-sought recording: Capt. Edward J. Ruppelt, first director of Project Blue Book, briefing on the reorganisation of the Air Force's UFO investigation. He states that of roughly 800 cases about 20% remained unexplained after technical analysis, notes that reports clustered near nuclear weapons facilities, and describes silent high-speed flight with radar-indicated speeds between 1,000 and 3,500 mph.

records.title: Unresolved UAP Report, Colorado, October 2023
records.aaro_description: Smartphone footage submitted by a law enforcement officer showing red, blue and green flashing lights, reported as silent. AARO cautions that phone autofocus and automated image processing may distort apparent shape and motion, particularly at high magnification.

records.title: Unresolved UAP Report, Colorado, October 2023
records.aaro_description: Second of four Colorado law-enforcement clips; rear-facing smartphone camera, digitally altered to protect privacy. Same red/blue/green flashing lights, reported silent.

records.title: Unresolved UAP Report, Colorado, October 2023
records.aaro_description: Third Colorado clip; a light source kept centre-frame at increasing magnification.

records.title: Unresolved UAP Report, Colorado, October 2023
records.aaro_description: Fourth Colorado clip; a largely stationary light source, with focus shifts caused by passing vehicles.
